title: Pendulum

caveats: animated illustration with no physical scale

slow_motion.evidence: No on-screen text or narration indicates slow motion; motion appears continuous in real time.

subjects.description: Small green circular pendulum bob hanging from a thin black string under a dark horizontal bar.

observation.what_happens: A green ball hanging from a string swings side to side below a dark horizontal support. It starts displaced to the right, swings through the center toward the left, and continues oscillating for the whole clip.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: Theta oscillates at ~0.15 rad with period ~1.17 s on a clean 255 px circle, so it is a rigid pendulum with L ~0.34 m from T=2*pi*sqrt(L/g). Amplitude slowly falls from 0.152 to ~0.13 rad, suggesting weak damping in air. Candidates compare undamped small-angle vs full sin with linear viscous damping vs quadratic air drag.

critique.finding: The ball swings as a pendulum with length {L} pulled by gravity {g}. It loses a little swing energy each moment to friction {b}.
critique.headline: Green ball swings steadily as gentle friction slowly steals motion
critique.why_it_won: It matches the even shrinking of the swings while quadratic air drag shrinks fast swings too much and slow swings too little.

headline: Green ball swings steadily as gentle friction slowly steals motion
finding: The ball swings as a pendulum with length 0.35 ± 6.66e-5 m pulled by gravity 9.81 m/s². It loses a little swing energy each moment to friction 0.0792 ± 9.86e-4 1/s.

eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle pendulum obeys theta_ddot + b*theta_dot + (g/L)*sin(theta)=0, so period T approx 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) gives L from timing, and amplitude envelope decays as exp(-b*t/2) giving b from decay.
